title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra for computer-use workloads
dek: A lower-priced model prioritizes visual understanding and tool-driven desktop tasks over frontier reasoning per token.
evidence: OpenAI vendor benchmark and price disclosures, not an independent ranking
takeaway: Compare cost and successful completion across identical computer-use tasks before substituting a cheaper model.

sections.title: Model trade-off

bullets.detail: Standard API prices are $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. Its token prices differ from total workflow cost.
OpenAI reports improved computer use and visual reasoning versus GPT-5.6 Terra, with deployments in Work, Codex and the API rather than general ChatGPT conversation.

paragraphs: API pricing: Standard API prices are $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens and $5 per million output tokens. Its token prices differ from total workflow cost.
Positioning: OpenAI reports improved computer use and visual reasoning versus GPT-5.6 Terra, with deployments in Work, Codex and the API rather than general ChatGPT conversation.

sections.title: Evaluation

bullets.detail: At medium effort, OpenAI cites a 15-percentage-point gain on Agents' Last Exam versus GPT-5.6 Terra at roughly one-third of the cost; this is a vendor comparison.
Use a frozen set of visual navigation, form entry, spreadsheet and tool-recovery tasks; measure cost per verified task, p95 duration and unauthorized-action attempts.
